pediatricPearls: Use pediatric dosing of medications or electrical therapy for a pediatric patient < 37 kg and as defined HandTevy
Children compensate well initially but decompensate quickly with little warning.
Most pediatric cardiac arrests are due to respiratory compromise.

pl1: Apply high-flow Oxygen to both the tracheostomy and the face
BVM – connect to tracheostomy with inner cannula, or pediatric mask if unable
> If no chest rise, block tracheostomy with wet gauze and BVM on face
Look for easily correctible causes of distress, such as detached oxygen sources
If ventilator problem, remove patient from ventilator and utilize BVM
If no pulse at any time, CPR
pl3: If suction catheter cannot be passed, ventilate from mouth with standard airway management while covering stoma
pl4: > 2-3mL saline may be used to loosen secretions
IV / IO access as appropriate for patient condition
If bleeding profusely, place 20cc of air or saline into cuff
pl5: If tube is blocked, deflate cuff if present and remove/clean or attempt to place new one
Attempt oral intubation Replace stoma with ETT (one size below tracheostomy size or 6.0) Direct the placement of digital pressure on the posterior wall of the manubrium
> If this requires removal of the tracheostomy tube, only perform after successful intubation (will need to go deeper)
